data.title: Revolve Enters into Definitive Agreement to Acquire Three Project, 6 MW Battery Storage Portfolio in Ontario
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Revolve Renewable Power Corp. (CSE:REVV)(OTCQB:REVVF) ("Revolve" or the "Company"), a North American owner, operator and developer of power generation and digital infrastructure projects, is pleased to announce that, through a subsidiary, it has entered into a definitive agreement for the acquisition (the "Acquisition") of all of the issued and outstanding shares in the capital of Logan Energy Storage ULC ("Logan"). Logan owns a portfolio of three battery energy storage system ("BESS") projects located in Ontario (the "Portfolio"), with a total capacity of 6 megawatts ("MW") / 11.7 MWh. The total purchase price for the Portfolio is CAD$1,500,000 and will be funded by cash on the Company's balance sheet. The seller of the Logan is arm's length to Revolve.

The Company executed definitive equity purchase and related agreements October 30, 2026, providing for the Acquisition, which remains subject to customary closing conditions and applicable approvals. Upon closing, the Acquisition is expected to increase Revolve's battery storage capacity in Ontario to approximately 20.2 MW / 36.0 MWh across nine projects. It builds on the Company's acquisition of the six-project, 14.2 MW / 24.3 MWh Trillium Storage portfolio, completed in August 2026.

"The Logan acquisition is another important step for Revolve as we continue to build our storage platform in Ontario," said Myke Clark, CEO. "Following the completion of Trillium, this transaction is expected to increase our battery storage capacity in the province and further establish our presence in Ontario. We look forward to closing the transaction and building on this platform as we continue to execute our disciplined acquisition and development strategy."

The transaction reflects Revolve's continued strategy of acquiring assets alongside its greenfield development pipeline.

About Revolve

Revolve was formed in 2012 to capitalize on the growing global demand for renewable power. Revolve develops utility-scale wind, solar, hydro and battery storage projects in the US, Canada and Mexico. Revolve also installs and operates sub 20 megawatt ("MW") "behind the meter" distributed generation (or "DG") assets. Revolve's portfolio includes the following:

  • Operating Assets: 36.2 MW (net) of operating assets under long-term power purchase and services agreements across the US, Canada and Mexico covering wind, solar, battery storage and hydro generation;
  • Development: a diverse portfolio of utility scale development projects across the US, Canada and Mexico with a combined capacity of over 3,000MWs as well as a 140MW+ distributed generation portfolio that is under development.

Revolve has an accomplished management team with a demonstrated track record of taking projects from "greenfield" through to "ready to build" status and successfully concluding project sales to large operators of utility-scale renewable energy projects. To-date, Revolve has developed and sold over 1,550MW of projects.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. (the "Company" or "Prospect Ridge") (CSE:PRR)(OTCQB:PRRSF)(FRA:0ED) is pleased to announce that it has closed the third and final tranche of its non-brokered private placement (the "Offering") of $0.075 critical mineral flow-through units (the "FT Units") first announced on October 2, 2026, and updated on October 13th, 19th and 21st, 2026 (see news releases for details), issuing an aggregate of 2,016,669 FT Units for gross proceeds of $151,250.18. All securities issued in the third tranche are subject to a statutory hold period expiring on March 1, 2027.

Each FT Unit was comprised of one flow-through common share (a "Common Share") in the capital of the Company and one-half of one Common Share purchase warrant (each whole warrant, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one common share at a price of $0.10 for a period of two years after closing, subject to accelerated expiry if the Company's common shares trade or close on the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "Exchange") at $0.21or more for ten consecutive trading days.

In connection with the third tranche, the Company paid aggregate finder fees of $8,487.51 in cash and issued an aggregate of 113,167 finder warrants having the same terms as the warrants comprised in the FT Units (exercisable at $0.10 for two years subject to acceleration on the occurrence of certain events). There was no insider participation in the third tranche.

Over the three tranches, the Company raised aggregate gross proceeds of $1,836,375 through the issue of 24,485,004 FT Units, representing an oversubscription of $336,375 over the originally planned Offering of $1,500,000.

Over the three tranches, insiders purchased an aggregate of 335,000 FT Units, which as of the third tranche closing represented less than 1% of the then issued and outstanding shares, and less than 1% if the associated warrants were immediately exercised. The participation by insiders constitutes a "related party transaction" within the meaning of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The Company has relied upon the exemption from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements pursuant to sections 5.5(a), (b) and (c), and sections 5.7(1)(a) and (b), respectively, of MI 61-101.

Use of Proceeds of the Offering

The Company intends to use the gross proceeds from the FT Shares to incur, on its mineral projects in British Columbia, eligible "Canadian exploration expenses" that will also qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" under the Income Tax Act. The Company intends the bulk of the gross proceeds to finance an upcoming 2,500-meter drill program on the Issuer's Camelot project, located near Horsefly, B.C. (see News Releases dated January 23, February 25 and June 16, 2026) and for preparations for an extensive Spring drill program at the Company's Excalibur project located north of Smithers, B.C (see News Releases dated September 10 and 24, 2026).

The securities to be offered under the Offering have not been, and will not be, registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act") or any U.S. state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, United States persons absent registration or any applicable exemption from the registration requirements of the U.S. Securities Act and applicable U.S. state securities laws. This news release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy securities in the United States, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful.

Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. is a British Columbia-based exploration and development company focused on critical metals and gold. Led by a seasoned management and technical team with over 100 years of combined mineral exploration experience, Prospect Ridge is advancing its north-central B.C. located Golden Horseshoe and Cariboo projects - high-potential copper-gold systems positioned within one of Canada's most under-explored yet geologically endowed mineral belts.

Hot Chili Limited - Quarterly Report, Period Ending 30 September 2026

PR Newswire

PERTH, Australia, Oct. 30, 2026

PERTH, Australia, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

Highlights

Second Porphyry Discovery Confirmed at La Verde

  • Assay results for step-out drilling, completed after the reporting period, confirmed the discovery of a second porphyry center – La Verde South - near-doubling the growth potential of the La Verde Project.
  • First step-out Reverse Circulation (RC) drill hole DKP084, located approximately 250 m to the south of La Verde's +0.4% Cu mineralisation footprint, has delivered:
    • 148 m grading 0.44% CuEq1 (0.39% Cu, 0.07 g/t Au) from 36 m

  • First step-out diamond drill hole (DD) DKD100, located a further 100 m to the south of DKP084, also visually recorded a 307 m down-hole interval of copper porphyry-style mineralisation2.
  • Phase 2 resource infill and extensional drilling for La Verde is now complete, following 13 months and over 40,000m of DD and RC drilling, adding to the 10,000 m of RC drilling from Phase 1.

Hot Chili Delivers More Copper-Gold at La Verde

  • Strong assay results continued to be delivered during the quarter from the four drill rigs (2 Diamond and 2 Reverse Circulation) located at La Verde.
  • Continuity of higher-grade copper-gold mineralisation from shallow depths was further confirmed from infill drilling and step out diamond drilling continued to expand the discovery footprint.
  • Standout results reported during the quarter included:
    • DKP063 recorded 398 m grading 0.45% CuEq (0.35% Cu, 0.12 g/t Au) from surface
      • Including 62 m grading 0.91% CuEq (0.70% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au) from 20 m
      • Which includes 34 m grading 1.00% CuEq (0.80% Cu, 0.27 g/t Au) from 42 m
    • DKD060 recorded 472 m grading 0.41% CuEq (0.34% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au) from 49 m
      • Including 105.8 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.58% Cu, 0.15 g/t Au) from 397 m
      • Including 32.6 m grading 0.90% CuEq (0.75% Cu, 0.19 g/t Au) from 438 m
    • DKP064 recorded 126 m grading 0.45% CuEq (0.38% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au) from 54 m
      • Including 26 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.60% Cu, 0.13 g/t Au) from 108 m
    • DKP078 recorded 240 m grading 0.43% CuEq (0.30% Cu, 0.17 g/t Au) from 36 m
      • Including 54 m grading 0.60% CuEq (0.41% Cu, 0.26 g/t Au) from 46 m
      • And including 42 m grading 0.50% CuEq (0.36% Cu, 0.20 g/t Au) from 188 m
  • The maiden La Verde MRE, revised Costa Fuego PFS and preparation of the EIA submission remained on track, with assay results pending for 35 drill holes (24 infill drilling and 11 southern step-out drillholes).

La Verde Drilling Totals 50,000m, with Phase 2 Now Complete

Strong Cash Position of A$29.3 Million following closure of OR Royalty Amendment Agreement during the quarter.

View PDF version

SUMMARY OF OPERATIONAL ACTIVITIES

Second Porphyry Centre Confirmed at La Verde South

Assay results for step-out drilling, returned after the reporting period, confirmed the discovery of a second porphyry centre at La Verde South. Located immediately south of, and along strike from, the initial La Verde copper-gold porphyry discovery, extending the potential mineralisation footprint of La Verde to 1,400m.

The first Reverse Circulation (RC) step-out drill hole, DKP084, was collared approximately 250 m south of La Verde's existing +0.4% Cu mineralisation footprint and returned 148 m grading 0.44% CuEq1 (0.39% Cu, 0.07 g/t Au) from 36 m, including 44 m grading 0.56% CuEq (0.50% Cu, 0.06 g/t Au) from 138 m.

The intersection was primarily oxide copper porphyry-style mineralisation, commencing immediately below shallow gravel cover, and was designed to follow up previously reported RC drill hole DKP024, which recorded 114 m grading 0.4% CuEq (0.4% Cu) from 86 m, including 52 m grading 0.5% CuEq (0.5% Cu, 0.1 g/t Au) from 96 m (see announcement dated 19 May 2025).

The first southern Diamond Drill (DD) step-out drill hole, DKD100, was then collared a further 100 m south of DKP084 to test for higher-grade copper porphyry-style sulphide mineralisation beneath the oxide zone.

DKD100 visually recorded a 307 m downhole interval of copper porphyry-style mineralisation2, comprising oxide mineralisation between 40 m and 172 m and porphyry-style sulphide mineralisation between 172 m and 347 m.

Core photo from DKD100 (259 – 261 m downhole) with vein-hosted and disseminated chalcopyrite (2%) and pyrite (4%) mineralisation in strongly veined tonalite host rock2


1 Copper Equivalent (CuEq) reported for the drillhole intersections were calculated using the following formula: CuEq% = ((Cu% × Cu price 1% per tonne × Cu_recovery) + (Mo ppm × Mo price per g/t × Mo_recovery) + (Au ppm × Au price per g/t × Au_recovery) + (Ag ppm × Ag price per g/t × Ag_recovery)) / (Cu price 1% per tonne × Cu_recovery). The Metal Prices applied in the calculation were: Cu=4.50 USD/lb, Au=3,150 USD/oz, Mo=20 USD/lb, and Ag=30 USD/oz. Sampling methodologies are described in the attached JORC Table 1.

Expansion Drilling Continues to Demonstrate Scale and Continuity

In parallel with southern step-out drilling, drilling across the main La Verde discovery continued to refine the geological interpretation of the mineralised system, further delineating the interpreted high-grade core and demonstrating the vertical and lateral continuity of porphyry-hosted copper-gold mineralisation.

A significant result was returned from DKD060 intersected 472 m grading 0.41% CuEq (0.34% Cu, 0.08g/t Au) from 49 m depth, including a significant higher-grade component comprising 105.8 m grading 0.70% CuEq from 397 m, which also included 32.6 m grading 0.90% CuEq from 438 m (Figure 4).

Results from RC drill hole DKP067 also expanded the lateral extent of mineralisation along La Verde's eastern flank. The drillhole, reported as a partial result, returned 112 m grading 0.47% CuEq (0.40% Cu, 0.10 g/t Au) from 42 m, including 26 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.59% Cu, 0.14 g/t Au) from 62 m.

In-fill RC Drilling Confirms Continuity of Near-Surface, Bulk Mineralisation

RC drill holes targeting the up-dip extension of high-grade mineralisation at La Verde has continued to return wide intersections of copper-gold mineralisation from shallow depths. Importantly, results are distributed across the deposit, highlighting the scale and continuity of La Verde's growing high-grade core.

These results are headlined by DKP063 (Figure 4), which recorded 398 m grading 0.45% CuEq (0.35% Cu, 0.12 g/t Au) from surface. Within this, a significant higher-grade component includes 62 m grading 0.91% CuEq (0.70% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au) from just 20 m depth, demonstrating the continuity of high-grade mineralisation at shallow depths and reinforcing the potential for a high-grade starter pit, capable of delivering early higher-grade material to the Costa Fuego mine plan.

DKP075 recorded a partial result of 132 m grading 0.57% CuEq (0.45% Cu, 0.16 g/t Au) from 24 m depth which included 42 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.57% Cu, 0.19 g/t Au) from 96 m (Figure 5). Results for the final 177 m were still outstanding and are expected to be reported shortly.

Additionally, DKP064, which was collared at the southern extent of La Verde's high-grade core, returned 126 m grading 0.45% CuEq (0.38% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au) from 54 m depth, including 26 m grading 0.70% CuEq (0.60% Cu, 0.13 g/t Au) from 108 m, together with a second intersection of 74 m grading 0.35% CuEq (0.29% Cu, 0.07 g/t Au) from 276 m.

La Verde Drilling Totals 50,000m, with Phase 2 Now Complete

Drilling for the 40,000 m Phase 2 DD and RC program is now complete, following 13 months of progress and bringing the total at La Verde to 50,000 m. The Phase 1 RC program (completed from late 2024 to mid-2025) included 10,000 m and outlined a 750 m x 400 m x 400 m footprint, and in conjunction with Phase 2, has now identified a 1,400 m x 780 m x 800 m footprint across two porphyry centres. Resource infill drilling of La Verde is now complete, and drill rigs will start back up and focus on the growth of La Verde South in early 2027.

Project Development Integration

Since 30 June 2026, Hot Chili has further strengthened the dedicated Costa Fuego project development team and its integrated governance framework for the revised Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) and Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) programs, progressing multiple engineering, permitting, social, infrastructure and technical studies.

Key activities advanced include mine-plan inputs, hydrogeological and geotechnical investigations, TSF engineering and water-management studies, and evaluation of power-supply and transmission-line relocation options. Project controls are being consolidated through an integrated P6 schedule, clearer critical-path reporting, risk management and disciplined contractor cost and payment controls.

Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) Continue to Progress

During the quarter preparation of the Costa Fuego environmental approvals continued under the separate EIA 1A (Huasco Water) and EIA 1B (Costa Fuego) workstreams. Unusually heavy rainfall during July and August 2026 affected field activities resulted in delays which have been mitigated in part through four weeks of scheduled contingency. The Q2 2027 submission remains on track for both EIAs.

The two-stream permitting strategy has now been embedded in the project delivery framework:

  • EIA 1A: the seawater intake, pumping and distribution system. Work progressed on the Project Description, environmental chapters, PAS 155 and PAS 156 gap-closure actions, the Punta Huasco Sur protection-area consultation, and flora, vegetation, vertebrate fauna and entomofauna compatibility studies. The latest Project Description revision was under review in October.
  • EIA 1B: baseline studies, engineering inputs and environmental documentation progressed in parallel with the revised PFS2. Archaeological fieldwork was completed, hydrogeological field investigations and packer testing advanced, and the TSF, diversion-water and associated infrastructure packages continue to be developed for incorporation into the assessment.

Costa Fuego Revised PFS Advancement

During the quarter Hot Chili continued to advance workstreams at La Verde, designed to incorporate the new discovery into the Costa Fuego PFS as soon as possible. Geotechnical workstreams were completed at La Verde and are being incorporated into Mineral Resource Estimation and engineering design work, in parallel to metallurgical, hydrogeological and tailings testwork programs.

Analysis of multiple potential materials handling options between La Verde and Productora, the Costa Fuego central processing hub, are also underway. The potential development of a large open-pit mining scenario at Cortadera as an alternative to the previously defined open-pit and underground block cave operation for the later years of Costa Fuego's mine plan is also being finalised.

Social Integration and Community Support

Hot Chili continued its community engagement activities, with a round of early community engagement (Participación Ciudadana Temprana, PCT) in Huasco, Freirina and Vallenar. Public information stands shared details about the Huasco Water project and introduced the Produce Futuro Fund. Additional baseline interviews were completed with a further 9 parties, including 7 Indigenous organisations and 2 neighbourhood associations.

Launched in September, the Produce Futuro Fund will provide grants to successful applicants to support economic development in the Huasco Valley. Hot Chili coordinated the launch and held support sessions to help community members apply. The company received more than 300 applications, with 55 grants to be awarded next quarter.

SUMMARY OF CORPORATE ACTIVITIES

Strategic Partnering Process Update

Hot Chili continues to advance its asset-level strategic Partnering Process, aimed at introducing one or more qualified partners with the financial, technical and operational capability to assist in funding and delivery of the projects.

During the quarter management continued to facilitate ongoing due diligence activities, including arranging site visits, while discussions continued in relation to existing non-binding, indicative, incomplete and conditional proposals received for potential transactions involving the projects. 

The Partnering Process may result in a range of transactions for the Projects. Investors are cautioned that there is no certainty the Partnering Process will result in a transaction or binding agreement.

BMO Capital Markets continues to act as financial adviser in connection with the Partnering Process.

The Company will continue to update the market in accordance with its continuous disclosure obligations.

OR Royalty Amendment Agreement

During the quarter, Hot Chili completed the Amended and Restated Investment Agreement with OR Royalties Inc. ("OR"), receiving net proceeds of A$20.4 million, after transaction costs, from the additional US$15 million royalty investment.

The transaction brings total consideration received under the OR royalty arrangement to US$30 million and expands OR's royalty interest to include the La Verde Project.

The additional non-dilutive funding further strengthens the Company's balance sheet and supports the ongoing advancement of La Verde and the broader Costa Fuego copper-gold development.

The agreement also incorporates an updated change of control buy-back provision, preserving strategic flexibility as the Company progresses its Strategic Partnering Process.

For further details, refer to the Company's announcement dated 7 July 2026.

Cash Position

As of 30 September 2026, the Company had cash of A$29.3 million and no debt.

The operating expenditure for quarter ended 30 September 2026 included payments for staff costs of A$1.3 million and administration and corporate costs of A$1.5 million.

The investing expenditure for quarter ended 30 September 2026 included payments for tenements of A$3.4 million relating mostly to the payment of the San Antonio Purchase Option Agreement for US$2 million, and payments for exploration and evaluation of A$10.1 million relating to drilling (four drill rigs in operation) and development study activities across the La Verde copper-gold porphyry discovery, value engineering workstreams and EIA submission activities. Conceptual Open Pit Shells

Conceptual open pit shells represent Exploration Targets as defined in the 2012 Edition of the 'Australasian Code for Reporting of Exploration Results, Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves' (JORC Code). They are based on completed exploration activities reported in the announcement released 19 May 2025 ('Hot Chili Announces Latest Drill Results for La Verde, Doubling Porphyry Discovery Footprint').

The conceptual open pit shells were generated using copper (Cu) prices of US$3.50/lb Cu and US$6.00/lb Cu on a series of nested Cu grade shells. Other input parameters informing the conceptual open-pit shells (pit slope angles, mining cost, processing cost, etc.) were derived from values reported in the March 2025 Costa Fuego Pre-feasibility Study and are considered appropriate for the style of mineralisation encountered at the La Verde Cu-Au porphyry discovery.

Any potential quantity and grade of the Exploration Target shown is conceptual in nature. There has been insufficient exploration to estimate a Mineral Resource within the target area, and it is uncertain if further exploration will result in the estimation of a Mineral Resource.

Further exploration activities are detailed in this announcement and include (but may not necessarily be limited to) a program of diamond drill holes aiming to extend the mineralised footprint at La Verde. Drilling commenced on 22 September 2025, with the length of the program dependent on a number of considerations including (but not limited to) the results of the exploration activities and regulatory applications and approvals.

By Bill Peters

Okta is slated to join the index on Wednesday, replacing Kenvue

Okta shares have more than doubled this year.

Following a massive rise in its stock this year, workplace cybersecurity platform Okta has landed a spot on the S&P 500.

The company (OKTA) will join the benchmark stock index SPX before the opening of trading on Wednesday, S&P Dow Jones Indices said in a statement on Friday.

Okta shares were up 2.5% after hours in the wake of the news. The company will replace Kenvue (KVUE), the maker of Benadryl and Tylenol that's in the process of being acquired by Kimberly-Clark (KMB).

The change comes after a nearly 141% tear higher for Okta's stock so far this year. The company now has a market value of around $38.8 billion.

More broadly, annual revenue for the company has risen since 2017, according to FactSet data, alongside the rise of cloud services, mobile usage, remote work, artificial intelligence and AI agents.

"As AI agents transform every layer of technology, every agent needs a trusted identity and clear controls over what it can access and do," Okta CEO Todd McKinnon said in the company's earnings release in August.

The idea is that as businesses outsource more tasks to AI, they'll need to make sure that those AI tools have the credentials they need to access relevant applications - and that AI doesn't inadvertently get access to sensitive areas.

Cybersecurity stocks in general have had a strong year, with the Amplify Cybersecurity ETF HACK up 55% over the course of 2026 to date.

data.title: Humane Society of Southern Arizona Opens Client-Choice Pet Pantry, Among First in U.S.
data.description:
Humane Society of Southern Arizona Opens Client-Choice Pet Pantry, Among First in U.S.

Humane Society of Southern Arizona Opens Client-Choice Pet Pantry, Among First in U.S.

PR Newswire

TUCSON, Ariz., Oct. 30, 2026

Dart Mart opens to the public on Nov. 18 from 2 to 4 p.m.

TUCSON, Ariz., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Humane Society of Southern Arizona (HSSA) is opening the first client-choice pet pantry in Tucson, AZ, modeled on best practices from human food pantries. The updated on-site pet pantry venue, "Dart Mart," will officially open to the public on Nov. 18 from 2 to 4 p.m. at HSSA's main campus, 635 W. Roger Rd.

In client-choice "super-market" models, visitors choose their own items instead of receiving a pre-packed bag. The model dates to at least 1993, when New York City's West Side Campaign Against Hunger adopted it, and has spread to food pantries nationwide. It has yet to become common among pet pantries. A Feeding America study by NORC at the University of Chicago found that clients at full-choice pantries reported higher satisfaction, more variety, shorter waits, and less wasted food.

"I've worked in animal welfare a long time, and Dart Mart is one of only a handful like it in the country," said Michelle Dosson, Pacific Regional Director at Best Friends Animal Society and a member of HSSA's Board of Directors. "Food pantries learned decades ago that people know what their households need. Dart Mart at HSSA is the next chapter for dignity in animal welfare services, and I am so proud we are a part of it."

At Dart Mart, each household gets 300 points a month to spend. Every item has a point value, and an attendant helps with checkout. The pantry sees over 2,000 visits a year. The space is styled like a corner market, with colorful storefront windows.

Dart Mart is named for Dart, a beloved German Shepherd mix, by his person, L. Wilson, whose gift gave the space its name. She found him in 2015, when she saw him and his mother in busy traffic.

"I stopped and opened the car door, and both jumped in. It was apparent they were in trouble, hungry, and confused. Of course they came home with me," Wilson said. She took Dart to HSSA to be scanned for a microchip, vaccinated, and neutered. He showed signs of head trauma and managed multiple physical challenges throughout his life.

"Dart had a myriad of quirks which made me love him even more. Quite frankly, Dart was a magnificent dog. He was so loved, and I'm honored to share our love with other families in his memory," Wilson added.

Michele Figueroa, Chief Programs Officer at HSSA, started the Pet Pantry as it is known today when she joined the executive team three years ago. Figueroa has been spearheading the next evolution of this service, which is built on decades of food distribution efforts at the organization.

"People know their pets better than we do," said Figueroa. "If your dog needs a harness, you get to pick your favorite from what's on the shelf. If your cat loves a certain toy, grab it. Same with food: pick the kind your pet loves best. Our clients deserve the dignity of choice."

Dart Mart runs on donated goods. Greater Good Charities provided 90% of the food and supplies on its shelves.

"The Humane Society of Southern Arizona is leading the way in how pet pantries serve their communities," said Liz Baker, CEO of Greater Good Charities. "Dart Mart lets families choose the food and supplies their pets actually need, so every donation goes where it helps most. We're proud to support HSSA's Pet Pantry and to see them show up for Southern Arizona with such empathy and care."

Dart Mart is part of HSSA's Love Stays Home program, which helps families keep their pets rather than surrender them to shelters.

"A pet that stays home is a pet who does not need a kennel," said Dr. Kristin Barney, CEO of HSSA. "This is a success for the pet, the person, and the shelters. Love Stays Home runs on donations, and Dart Mart is a good example of what that support funds."

The pantry joins other efforts at HSSA to keep pets with their families, including last year's collaboration to enhance Pima County's Pet Support Center, funded by a $1.9M grant from Maddie's Fund.

Dart Mart also marks a launch within HSSA's 10,000 Acts of Love campaign. Pet food and supplies are welcome at HSSA, and gifts of any size help keep programs like Dart Mart open. To give, visit hssaz.org/donate. To learn more about Dart Mart, visit hssaz.org/pet-pantry.

About the Humane Society of Southern Arizona
Officially incorporated in 1944, the Humane Society of Southern Arizona is the oldest and largest animal welfare nonprofit in southern Arizona. Its mission is to compassionately serve pets and the people who love them. Learn more at hssaz.org, or visit 635 W. Roger Road, Tucson.

data.title: Fitch Lowers France's Outlook to Negative From Stable
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis 




  Fitch Ratings said it was lowering its outlook on France's credit rating to negative from Stable, while affirming the country's A+ ratings. 



  The move comes as France faces economic and social pressure over its debt and growing borrowing costs. In recent weeks, hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Paris and other French cities, with some protesters resorting to vandalism and violence. 



  Fitch said the negative outlook reflects a deterioration since its August review, and cited weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit. These factors are worsening debt dynamics from an already weak starting point, Fitch added. 



  Yields on France's government bonds have also risen since the last review, Fitch said. The agency said it now forecasts interest payments will increase to 3.3% of GDP in 2028 from 2.5% of GDP in 2025. Fitch also sees France's deficit at 5.5% of GDP in 2027, which it said reflects a weaker growth assessment and the risk of concessions during the budget process. 



  The country's A+ rating is supported by a large, wealthy and diversified economy, strong institutions, euro area membership and a resilient banking sector, Fitch added. 



  The next scheduled review date for France's rating hasn't yet been set, Fitch said, but added it expects to review the rating by end-February 2027 at the latest.

BKFC Founder David Feldman Steps Up for Harassed Michigan Worker with Donation and All-Expenses-Paid Family Cruise Invitation

Feldman invites Red Baron employee Walter Zerod and his family to join BKFSea as special guests, in solidarity against bullying and in support of hardworking Americans

Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) founder and president David Feldman is stepping up in a big way to support Walter Zerod, a Michigan Red Baron employee whose treatment by a streamer sparked national outrage and an outpouring of support. Feldman has pledged a personal donation to the growing fundraising effort and is going one step further, inviting Zerod and his family on an all-expenses-paid Caribbean getaway to BKFSea in January 2027.

BKFSea sets sail aboard Norwegian Jewel, traveling from Miami to Nassau, Bahamas. More than just a vacation, the one-of-a-kind experience will put Zerod and his family in the heart of the BKFC action, with live bare-knuckle fights at sea, exclusive opportunities to meet BKFC stars, nonstop entertainment and unforgettable experiences alongside fighters and fans.

Feldman was moved to act after learning about the worker’s experience through the GoFundMe campaign. According to the fundraiser, a streamer approached the employee and pretended to steal money using his phone, then laughed as the worker explained his distress. The campaign was launched to help provide financial support for the employee and his family amid uncertainty following the incident.

“We’re a combat sports organization, but there’s no place for bullying or humiliating someone who’s just trying to do their job,” said Feldman. “This man was working hard to provide for his family, and somebody decided his dignity was worth sacrificing for a few clicks. That’s wrong, and the moment I saw this, I had to respond. Nobody should have to endure humiliation while trying to earn a living.”

The donation and invitation reflect Feldman’s commitment to turning an act of disrespect into meaningful support. Along with helping to ease the family’s immediate financial pressure, he wants to welcome them into a BKFC community that stands up for people who deserve better.

“Our fans are as tough as they come, and they have big hearts,” Feldman continued. “We stand up for hardworking Americans, like Walter. We want them to enjoy themselves on the cruise, feel welcome and know that the entire BKFC family and community is in their corner.”

BKFSea is the ultimate combat sports cruise, bringing the excitement of Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) to the high seas for an unforgettable, one-of-a-kind fan experience. Taking place January 22–25, 2027, aboard the Norwegian Jewel, the three-night voyage sails from Miami to Nassau, Bahamas, combining live bare-knuckle fighting, exclusive fighter meet-and-greets, interactive fan experiences, live entertainment, nightlife and more. Designed to bring fans closer to the action and their favorite BKFC personalities than ever before, BKFSea delivers an immersive, action-packed getaway that blends world-class combat sports with the excitement of a Caribbean cruise. For more information and reservations, visit www.BKFSea.com⁠

Those wishing to support Walter and his family can visit the GoFundMe campaign.

About Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship

Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) is the first promotion allowed to hold a legal, sanctioned, and regulated bare knuckle event in the United States since 1889. Based in Philadelphia, and headed by President and former professional boxer David Feldman, BKFC is dedicated to preserving the historical legacy of bare knuckle fighting, while utilizing a specifically created rule set that emphasizes fighter safety. BKFC holds all of its bouts in a revolutionary circular four-rope ring, designed to encourage fast-paced and exciting bouts. The patented BKFC “Squared Circle” contains scratch lines, based on the Broughton Rules which governed bare knuckle fighting in the 19th century, and which requires fighters to “Toe the Line”: start every round face to face, and just inches apart.

In BKFC, only those fighters who are established professionals in boxing, MMA, kickboxing, or Muay Thai are allowed to compete. The referees and judges are required to have extensive professional combat sports experience. All fights are held under the auspices and control of an Athletic Commission. Unlike other fighting organizations and combat sports internationally which claim to be “bare knuckle”, but require wraps, tape, and gauze; BKFC is true to its word as fighters are not allowed to wrap their hands to within one inch of the knuckle. This makes BKFC unquestionably the truest form of bare knuckle fighting. BKFC is dedicated to not just creating the safest, most exciting, and highest-level bare-knuckle fighting organization in the world, it’s also leading the way for a new fully recognized professional combat sport. BKFC is truly the sport of the future, which fully respects its remarkable past.
